In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
consumers are willing to pay more for whole grain bread than other bread types and that this is unaffected by the provision of nutritional information.
consumers are not willing to pay more for bread that contains a specific health benefit but that consumers are WPP more for bread that is perceived as being healthier than white bread.
consumers are willing to pay for bread products with functional ingredients and that they react positively to the inclusion of health information on bread products.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
consumers are willing to pay more for whole grain bread than white bread and that consumers are willing pay more for whole grains than functional ingredients.
consumers are willing to pay more for whole grain bread and that they respond to information about health benefits but not to information on specific health benefits.
consumers are willing to pay a premium for a healthy product but that the health benefit information provided is less important than the product type itself.
The main takeaway from our work is that
consumers are willing to pay for health information but that this does not necessarily translate into higher willingness to pay for products that are perceived to be healthier.
consumers are willing to pay for bread with functional ingredients and that the provision of health and nutritional benefits can increase consumer willingness to pay.
consumers are willing to pay for bread with functional ingredients and are also responsive to health and nutrition information.
